# v0.2 input fixtures — not goldens

**These files are not goldens. They are not authoritative and they are not
frozen.** They are the deterministic *inputs* the v0.2 report generator signs
and verifies — candidate implementation inputs on an implementation-candidate
branch.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `origin-*-receipt.json` | Six locally signed DAGR MCP admission receipts — one per declared `subject_ref_origin` value, plus one that genuinely omits the field. |
| `trust-bundle.json` | The fixture trust bundle carrying the single fixture issuer key. |

All six receipts share one `subject_ref` on purpose. Six receipts that carry
the same subject reference and differ only in what they declare must still
disclose six different origins — that is the no-inference rule made into a
fixture.

They are signed by a fixture key derived from a fixed, published seed label
recorded in `tools/generate_dagr_report_v0_2_goldens.py`, so these bytes — and
every hash derived from them — reproduce exactly on any machine. That key has
no authority: it signs nothing outside this contract directory and appears in
no trust bundle other than this one.

Because the generator is deterministic, these files are byte-identical to what
it emits; `tests/test_dagr_report_v0_2_generator.py` proves that on every run.

## No reports here

No `*-report.json` and no `expectations.json` live in this directory, and none
may be added to it. Verification reports carry a `verifier_commit`, and a
committed report is a concrete claim about which implementation produced it.
No such claim can be made truthfully before the implementation merges.

Authoritative v0.2 report goldens are generated by the post-merge closure PR
into `../golden/`, with `verifier_commit` set to the exact implementation
squash-merge commit. See `../README.md` for the closure procedure.
